title: Scalar compatibility of the direct general-ring orientation
statement: Let D, ell, X, Y, f, d, n, A satisfy the following hypotheses: D is the global algebraically closed finite-field datum; ell is prime and different from its characteristic; X and Y are separated schemes of finite type over D.k; f is a separated D.k-morphism smooth of pure relative dimension d; n>=1; and A is a finite commutative ring killed by ell^n, and supply Noetherian structures, quasi-compactness and one compactification of f. Put P equal to the bottom Q_ell setting of [def-sp-general-ring-canonical-data]. There are a unital prime-ring identification e, a scalar/root-generator normalized coefficient-line comparison t, a direct ordinary dualizing orientation alpha, and actual smooth diagonal geometry G. The canonical dualizing-unit map u is invertible, as is the scalar exceptional comparison c; their maps satisfy c u^{-1} nu^*(alpha) = the prescribed scalar extension of P.diagonalDualizingObject. Alpha satisfies OrientationNormalized for G. This asserts the orientation clauses only and asserts neither the tensor formula nor exponent independence.

proof.text: Construct the bottom coefficient ring equivalence, the unital map to A, and the common-exponent generator-normalized coefficient line.

Construct the ordinary A orientation from the actual closed diagonal, normalized Rees specialization and inverse bundle integration. Extract the coordinate-normalized ordinary prime-power orientation from the unique diagonalDualizingObject, and identify its Rees normalization.

Apply normalizedOrientation_scalar at equal exponents and cancel orientation inverses. The ordinary dualizing scalar map is invertible by finite_smooth_dualizing_scalar. The bounded-below comparison-adjunction unit makes both dualizing-unit maps invertible.

Paste the site/scalar dualizing-unit square with the ordinary orientation square and the prime-power comparison equation. The abstract categorical assembly proves exceptional reduction invertibility and the exact orientation equation. Naturality of the intrinsic scalar-presentation isomorphism supplies the prescribed finiteGeneralRingOrientationExtension.

theorem finiteGeneralRingOrientation
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (hEll : ell ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f] [HasCompactification f]
    (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (hA : ((ell ^ n : ℕ) : A) = 0) :
    let P := finiteGeneralRingPrimeSetting D ell hEll n hn
    let hAU := congrArg (fun a : A ↦ (⟨a⟩ : ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) hA
    ∃ e : P.Ring ≃+* ULift.{u} (ZMod P.diagonalExponent),
    ∃ t : Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.CoefficientLineComparison
        (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u} (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e))
        P.diagonalExponent P.diagonalExponent P.diagonalExponent_annihilates hAU X,
    ∃ alpha : Etale.dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) f ≅
        Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.line (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) P.diagonalExponent hAU X d,
    ∃ geometry : Etale.FiniteRingSectionDeformation.Geometry d
        (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f),
    ∃ hunit : IsIso (finiteGeneralRingDualizingUnitMap (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) f),
      IsIso (finiteGeneralRingReduction P (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e) f) ∧
      finiteGeneralRingReduction P (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e) f ≫
          @inv _ _ _ _ (finiteGeneralRingDualizingUnitMap (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) f) hunit ≫
          (Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.comparison (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) X).map alpha.hom =
        (finiteGeneralRingOrientationExtension P (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e)
          hAU d f (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k)) t).hom ∧
      Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.OrientationNormalized (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)
        P.diagonalExponent (pow_pos P.coefficients.prime.out.pos P.level)
        hAU f d geometry (P.diagonalExponent_isUnit (f ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k)))) alpha
